scope: Three sequential warmed Edit-mode GPU renders per configuration of the same reconstructed 21.1766-second station take plus one-second tail. Two sources, one binaural head, 53 objects/564 triangles, 44.1 kHz. Low/High differ only in response step (2048/512). Full quality is FFT1024/hop256/one ray per bin/five bounces. Spectral smoke is FFT128/hop64/one bounce and is a separate workload. CPU values are earlier single runs from doppler-2026-10-06.json, not a simultaneous/repeated CPU baseline. No full-budget CPU spectral timing is claimed. Renderer wall excludes take open/hash, reconstruction and CLI compilation.
timingScope: CPU stopwatch durations, not GPU timestamp queries. GPU responsePreparationSeconds measures submission only; audioSeconds includes final PCM waits. Whole-job wall is the throughput comparison.

initial.scope: producer stopped; callback counters sampled at stop

beforeStop.scope: producer stopped; callback counters sampled at stop

final.scope: producer stopped; callback counters sampled at stop

live.scope: 20-second Editor scene run, scripted walk and head turns; no compilation during Play. IR/1024 response step. Counters sampled before stopping, then at producer completion. No guarantee for other loads or platforms. This scene check preceded the final small-FFT barrier fix; full FFT1024 offline hashes were unchanged after that fix.

limitations: Live still misses deadlines despite completing without queue exhaustion; underrun and late counters overlap and must not be added.
Worst-case path-filter storage is reserved, about 387 MB numeric working storage at the full station budget; this is not process memory.
One work item groups each pair; each output bin reduces its path groups serially. Further grouping/reduction/FFT scheduling and storage optimization remains.
Only Apple M5/Metal verified; DirectX and target standalone latency remain unverified.
The geometric preview remains unsuitable as an approved physics training teacher; training export/inference are not implemented.
The Metal compiler emits the advisory early-return and signed-modulo warnings listed in editorState; all kernels execute the documented checks and no shader errors were reported.
